<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXVIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|371}}</noinclude>receiuing vs, for three daies intreated vs courteously. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=8}}† And it chaunced that the father of Publius lay vexed vvith feuers and the bloudy flixe. Vnto whom Paul entred: and vvhen he had praied, and imposed hands on him, he healed him. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=9}}† Vvhich being done, al in the ile also that had infirmities, came, and vvere cured: {{verse|chapter=28|verse=10}}† who also honoured vs vvith many honours, and when vve vvere sailing away, laded vs vvith necessaries.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=11}}† And after three moneths, we sailed in a ship of Alexandria, that had wintered in the iland, vvhose signe vvas the Castors. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=12}}† And vvhen vve vvere come to Syracûsa, vve taried there three daies. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=13}}† Thence compassing by the shore, vve came to Rhegium: and after one day the South winde blovving, vve came the second day to Putéoli, {{verse|chapter=28|verse=14}}† vvhere finding brethren, vve were desired to tarie vvith them seuen daies: and so vve came to Rome. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=15}}† And from thence, vvhen the brethren had heard, they came to meete vs vnto ''Apij-forum'', and the Three-tauerns. Vvhom vvhen Paul had seen, giuing thanks to God, he tooke courage. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=16}}† And vvhen vve vvere come to Rome, Paul vvas permitted to remaine to him self with a souldiar that kept him. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=17}}† And after the third day he called together the cheefe of the Iewes. And vvhen they vvere assembled, he said to them, Men brethren, I doing nothing against the people, or the custome of the fathers, vvas deliuered prisoner from Hierusalem into the hands of the Romanes, {{verse|chapter=28|verse=18}}† who vvhen they had examined me, vvould haue released me, for that there vvas no cause of death in me. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=19}}† But the Ievves contradicting it, I vvas compelled to appeale vnto Cæsar, not as hauing any thing to accuse my nation. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=20}}† For this cause therfore I desired to see you and to speake to you. for, because of the hope of Israël, am I compassed vvith this {{sup|‖}} chaine.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=21}}† But they said to him, Vve neither receiued letters concerning thee from Iewrie, neither did any of the brethren that came hither, report or speake any euil of thee. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=22}}† But vve desire of thee to heare vvhat thou thinkest: for {{sup|‖}} concerning this {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ αἱρέσεως.}}∷ secte, it is knowen to vs that it is gainesaid euery vvhere. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=23}}† And vvhen they had appointed him a day, they came to him vnto his lodging very many: to vvhom he expounded, testifying the kingdom of God, and vsing persuasion to them<noinclude>{{rh||Aaa ij|of}}</noinclude>
